description: Measured fixed-state timing and validation comparisons. Mission results are separate.
findings: The planner already uses an outer JIT, scan over diffusion iterations and horizon, and batched field/trajectory rollouts.
CPU-only JAX. Timings synchronize results; compilation is separate.
Dominant reduction is fewer diffusion proposals and a coarser planning/control interval, not a claimed JAX rewrite.
The 2D Newton solve is algebraically fused. Its complete-planner speed improvement alone is small.
Changing batch width alone did not improve measured time and caused sensitive float32 rollout costs to differ; rejected as a standalone optimization.
Eight projected Newton iterations are a finite-budget approximation. Fused and previous solvers match; both have small residual optimality gaps at some active box faces.
tests: 24 targeted checks passed; double precision matrix solve, previous projection solver, independent convex minimization, MBD and nonlinear 100 Hz execution.

timing_conditions: Local CPU under normal desktop use. Fixed-state benchmarks run without concurrent simulation jobs. The early reversed-wind mission calls overlapped local replay publication; raw mission timings retain that overhead. No hard real-time claim.
